defaultValue: Feel the time without reading the screen. Start with Terse Quarter at Standard speed; it reports the start of the current quarter hour. Your existing saved choices are kept. Use the guide below before choosing an exact-minute language.

items.defaultValue: Weather · Set up in three steps

1. Choose Enable weather below, then Save settings. PulseTime will ask the Pebble phone app for your location. The phone controls its permission prompt; allow location there if asked. Time and lessons work without location.

2. Location is used only for weather you request. An approximate position is sent to Open-Meteo to get rain forecasts. No location history is saved. Turn weather off here to stop requests. You can also change Pebble’s location access in your phone settings.
Location has not been checked yet.

3. On your watch, hold Select → Signals → Weather. Hold Select to refresh. If access was denied, allow location for the Pebble app in phone settings and try again. Keep the phone connected. Bluetooth pairing is handled by the Pebble app; no account or token is needed for weather.
Start here · Learn one pattern

1. Open PulseTime. A first-use guide appears on a normal launch. Later, hold Select and choose Learn pattern. Select plays an example; press it again to stop. Down moves forward, Up moves back, and Back returns. In the default language, 3:32 feels like 3:30: three hour pulses, a pause, then two longer quarter-hour pulses.

2. Learn the pause. At 3:00 the whole-time pattern has three hour pulses and no quarter pulses. At 3:30 it adds two quarter pulses. Exact minutes is off at first: 3:30 through 3:44 all feel the same. Turning exact minutes on adds two short ticks for 3:32.

3. In the clock screen, press Select for the whole time (or to stop playback), Up for the hour phrase, or Down for the minute phrase. Hold Select for Learn pattern, Practice, Language, Speed, Display, Quick Launch, and Status. Hold Up or Down is also a language shortcut. Back always takes you out.

Learn the whole-time pattern first. In minutes-only Terse Quarter, no quarters is one 300 ms pulse, while one quarter is 320 ms. These are very close. Use Select for the whole time when unsure; avoid a minutes-only Quick Launch until you have compared both on your wrist.
Display · Large and clear

items.label: Time size
items.defaultValue: bold
items.description: Bold gives the time more space. Both layouts fit rectangular and round watches.

items.label: Contrast
items.defaultValue: bright
items.description: Choose the contrast you read most easily. Bright changes the display colors; backlight brightness is controlled by your watch.

items.defaultValue: Haptic language · Choose by feel

items.label: Language
items.defaultValue: terse_quarter

options.label: Decimal Place · try for exact minutes

items.description: Terse Quarter is the simplest place to start. For exact time, try Decimal Place: hours, minute tens, then minute ones. Binary is shortest in the timing audit but requires reading bits. Familiarity matters more than speed; compare known examples in Practice before changing your daily language.

items.label: Playback speed
items.defaultValue: standard
items.description: Start at Standard. Slow makes pulses and pauses 25% longer; Fast makes them about 22% shorter. Some short ticks may be hard to feel on your watch. Choose by touch after comparing the same example.

items.label: Exact minutes (Terse Quarter only)
items.description: Adds short ticks for the minutes after the last quarter: 3:32 is three hour pulses, two quarter pulses, then two ticks. Up to 14 ticks may be needed. Only Terse Quarter uses this switch; all other languages already report exact minutes. It is also the second choice in the watch language menu.

items.defaultValue: Five-Minute Ladder counts hours, five-minute groups, then leftover minutes. Decimal Place uses a double-length pulse for a zero digit. Binary reads 4 hour bits then 6 minute bits, largest first (short 0, long 1). Nearest-Quarter names a nearby quarter and an offset; its hour phrase may name the next hour. Morse spells the 12-hour clock digits. None of these patterns distinguishes AM from PM.
Quick Launch · Set up side buttons

On your watch, open Settings > Quick Launch > Up (or Down) and choose PulseTime. This is a watch setting: PulseTime cannot assign or replace the shortcut for you. Then return to your watchface and hold that button to feel the time. Start with The whole time.

items.label: Up shortcut answer
items.defaultValue: full

items.label: Down shortcut answer
items.defaultValue: full

Pebble Time 2, Pebble 2 Duo, and Pebble Round 2 report which shortcut opened PulseTime, so each can play a different phrase. Pebble 2 SE, Pebble 2 HR, Pebble Time, and the original Time Round do not: either shortcut plays the whole time. Once PulseTime is open, Up and Down work for hour and minute phrases on every supported model. These choices do not assign the system shortcut.
Optional · Sound

On Pebble Time 2 and Pebble 2 Duo, sound can play the rhythm as pitched notes. Hours and different minute fields use different pitches. Pebble 2 SE and round watches have no supported speaker. Sound starts off and follows the watch mute setting; vibration remains available when sound cannot play.

items.label: Play sound
items.defaultValue: off
Sound is optional. This build uses the exported timing-based motor API; per-step strength awaits SDK support.
Optional · Chimes

Chimes briefly open PulseTime, play the time, then return you to your watchface. They work even when PulseTime is closed. On the hour you hear or feel the hour phrase; half-hour and quarter-hour chimes play the whole time. No background worker is needed.

items.label: Chime
items.defaultValue: off

Quiet hours silence automatic chimes only. Asking for the time always works. Set both ends to the same hour for no quiet period. The watch books up to eight future chimes and refills them on each launch. Status shows how many are actually booked.
Optional · Flick to tell time

items.label: Flick to tell time
items.description: Tap the watch twice along the same axis within about a second. PulseTime opens, tells the time, then returns to your watchface. This needs a continuously running accelerometer worker and uses battery. Pebble has one worker slot shared by all apps, so another app may block it or take it back. Status shows whether it is running. Leave this off and use Quick Launch if a side button works for you.

defaultValue: A different duration sequence is not proof that every pulse is easy to distinguish. Practice on your own watch. Start with whole-time playback and Standard speed, then choose the language and contrast you understand most reliably.

items.defaultValue: Advanced · Fixed place and data feeds

Optional. Weather normally uses this phone’s location. Choose Fixed place only to forecast somewhere else. Custom data feeds are for people who manage an HTTPS source; they are not needed for time or weather.

items.label: Weather location
items.defaultValue: phone
Custom feeds receive explicit requests only. Optional custom credentials stay on this phone. A failed or old reading becomes Unknown.
